content.overview: Radicle emergence is not the end of propagation. Seedling establishment depends on a root zone that balances water and air, stable identity, sanitary handling and early recognition of abnormal development.

sections.title: Establishment is a separate outcome
sections.body: A germinated seed can still fail during emergence or early seedling growth. Track normal establishment separately from radicle emergence.

sections.title: Root-zone moisture and aeration interact
sections.body: Propagation media must support water availability while retaining air-filled pore space. Persistent saturation or poor structure can create root stress and disease-favorable conditions.

sections.title: Sanitation protects interpretation and stock
sections.body: Dirty tools, reused contaminated surfaces, splash movement and mixed tray identity can convert a seedling-performance problem into a biosecurity and traceability problem.

commonMistakes: Treating a research protocol value as a universal production target.
Reporting successful seedlings without preserving the original denominator.
Changing multiple variables at once and then claiming one caused the result.
content.practicalApplication: Inspect a simulated seedling tray record and classify observations into identity, emergence, root-zone, sanitation and plant-health categories before proposing any cause.
content.summary: Use source-controlled evidence, preserve identity and denominators, and keep observations separate from explanations.
